title: ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ Spotted with 16 DDR5 Slots for Diamond Rapids
gist: ASRock Rack showed a single-socket Diamond Rapids Xeon board at OCP Summit 2026 with 16 DDR5 channels (1DPC) and no PCIe CEM slots or OCP NIC 3.0 connector, routing all 128 lanes of PCIe Gen6/CXL 3.0 through 16 MCIO x8 cable connectors. STH reads it as a clear sign that PCIe Gen6 signaling is forcing servers toward cabled I/O.

insights.claim: Intel's Diamond Rapids Xeon platform supports sixteen-channel memory, and ASRock Rack's single-socket DMRD16-2L+ board implements it with 16 DDR5 slots at one DIMM per channel on a 12x13-inch EEB form factor.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: Sixteen channels per socket raises DRAM content per server, a tailwind for DDR5/MRDIMM suppliers.

insights.claim: The DMRD16-2L+ supports RDIMMs up to 128GB at 8000MT/s, MRDIMMs up to 128GB at 12800MT/s, and 2U MRDIMM modules up to 256GB at 12800MT/s, implying up to 4TB of memory on a single socket with 256GB modules.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: MRDIMM at 12800MT/s becomes a mainstream server memory SKU with Diamond Rapids, shifting mix toward higher-ASP modules.
insights.quote: MRDIMMs up to 128GB at max 12800MT/s, and MRDIMM 2U modules up to 256GB
insights.locator: ASRock Rack says it supports three

insights.claim: The DMRD16-2L+ exposes up to 16 MCIO x8 connectors, each rated for PCIe 6.0 or CXL 3.0, totaling 128 lanes of Gen6/CXL 3.0 connectivity from one socket.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: High lane counts plus CXL 3.0 support enable memory-expansion and accelerator attach on single-socket servers.
insights.quote: So that is 128x PCIe Gen6 / CXL 3.0 lanes worth.
insights.locator: On the board, we have lots

insights.claim: The board omits both traditional PCIe CEM card slots and an OCP NIC 3.0 connector, so all of a host server's PCIe Gen6 I/O must run through MCIO cables.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: Server designs are shifting from slot-based risers to cabled backplanes, changing the bill of materials.
insights.quote: this does not have an OCP NIC 3.0 connector, nor traditional PCIe CEM slots

insights.claim: PCIe signal-integrity problems that began with Gen4 on Ice Lake have escalated with Gen6, making cables rather than PCB traces the preferred way to route high-speed I/O.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: Beneficiaries are high-speed cable/connector makers (MCIO-type interconnects) as Gen6 platforms ramp.
insights.quote: with Gen6, we can see clear signs of the move to more cables

insights.claim: ASRock Rack chose the ASPEED AST2700 BMC for management of its Diamond Rapids board, alongside an Intel I350 for dual 1GbE and a Realtek RTL8211F dedicated IPMI port.
insights.speaker: John Lee
insights.so_what: Confirms ASPEED's BMC design-win continuity into next-gen Intel server platforms.
